title: Transmission Control System Malfunction
shortDescription: TCM has detected an internal fault and requested MIL.
fullDescription:
P0700 is an informational code set by the PCM after the TCM (Transmission Control Module) reports any DTC. It indicates the transmission control system has a problem but does not by itself identify the failure.

Technicians must read TCM-specific sub-codes (e.g. P0730-P0799) to find the root cause. P0700 typically accompanies harsh shifting, slipping, or limp mode.
safetyImpact: Possible limp mode and unexpected loss of drive gears.

causes.cause: Wiring/connector issue between PCM and TCM

fixSteps.title: Pull TCM sub-codes
fixSteps.instruction: Use a bidirectional scanner to read transmission module DTCs.

fixSteps.title: Diagnose sub-code
fixSteps.instruction: Address the specific TCM DTC (e.g. P0750, P0731).

fixSteps.title: Clear and verify
fixSteps.instruction: Clear codes, road-test, confirm no return.

faq.a: Only briefly to a shop — limp mode and damage are likely.

title: Clutch Switch Input Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: PCM sees an invalid clutch pedal switch signal.
fullDescription:
P0704 sets when the manual transmission clutch position switch reports a value the PCM cannot reconcile with engine load and vehicle speed. It can disable cruise control and starter.

Common causes are a misadjusted switch, a broken plunger, or a corroded pedal harness.
safetyImpact: May prevent cruise control or cause hard starting.

fixSteps.title: Inspect switch
fixSteps.instruction: Check pedal switch alignment and plunger travel.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Fit new pedal switch, adjust per spec.

faq.a: Yes — typically only on manual transmission vehicles.

title: Transmission Range Sensor Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: Range sensor signal drops in and out.
fullDescription:
P0709 indicates the gear selector / range sensor signal is intermittently lost or invalid. The PCM cannot reliably know which gear position the driver has selected.

Corroded harness pins, an internal sensor failure, or loose linkage are typical causes.
safetyImpact: Possible no-start in Park, harsh engagement.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test
fixSteps.instruction: Move harness while live-data shows PRNDL.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Look for green corrosion, bent pins.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Fit new range sensor, adjust linkage.

faq.a: Often only when shifter is wiggled in Park or Neutral.

title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor Intermittent
shortDescription: TFT sensor signal drops in and out.
fullDescription:
P0714 is set when the transmission fluid temperature sensor reading goes intermittent — short open or short shifts that aren't caused by actual fluid behavior.

Usually a wiring or internal sensor fault. Can lock out torque converter clutch and skew shift schedules.
safetyImpact: Reduced fuel economy and potential overheating.

fixSteps.title: Live data sweep
fixSteps.instruction: Watch TFT during warm-up; flag dropouts.

faq.a: Short trips OK but get it diagnosed before long drives.

title: Output Speed Sensor Intermittent
shortDescription: OSS signal cuts out at random.
fullDescription:
P0723 sets when the output shaft speed sensor signal is intermittent. The TCM relies on OSS to compute gear ratio and torque converter slip; signal loss causes harsh shifts and false neutral events.

Most frequently caused by a bad sensor or chafed harness near the tail housing.
safetyImpact: Sudden loss of drive may occur.

fixSteps.title: Scan tool live data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare ISS vs OSS during drive.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check for damage near sensor mount.

fixSteps.title: Replace OSS
fixSteps.instruction: Fit new sensor, torque to spec.

faq.a: Yes — sustained false neutrals can damage clutches.

title: Brake Switch B Circuit High
shortDescription: Brake switch B input is high when it should not be.
fullDescription:
P0724 is set when the secondary brake switch (used for torque converter clutch unlock and shift logic) reports a continuous high signal. It can prevent TCC release on braking.

Commonly a stuck switch or shorted wire to power.
safetyImpact: TCC may not unlock at stops, potentially stalling.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Install new switch, adjust per spec.

faq.a: Often yes — common companion symptom.

title: Engine Speed Input Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: Engine speed signal to TCM is implausible.
fullDescription:
P0726 is set when the TCM receives an engine speed (RPM) value that disagrees with the expected range. The TCM uses this to compute torque converter slip and gear ratio.

Usually the result of a CKP signal issue, CAN bus dropout, or engine-side wiring fault.
safetyImpact: Erratic shifting and possible limp mode.

fixSteps.title: Compare RPM sources
fixSteps.instruction: Check engine RPM vs TCM RPM in scanner.

fixSteps.title: Repair source
fixSteps.instruction: Fix CKP, harness, or bus issue.

faq.a: Usually yes; the issue is the TCM seeing an odd RPM value.

title: Engine Speed Input Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: TCM engine speed input drops out intermittently.
fullDescription:
P0728 indicates the engine speed signal that feeds the TCM is intermittent. Brief dropouts can cause harsh shifts and false slip readings.

Look at CKP wiring, ground integrity, and CAN bus health.
safetyImpact: Intermittent harsh shifts may surprise the driver.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test
fixSteps.instruction: Move harness while watching live data.

faq.a: Similar root cause — P0728 is intermittent, P0726 is range/performance.

title: Incorrect Gear Ratio
shortDescription: TCM detects ratio outside spec for commanded gear.
fullDescription:
P0730 sets when the calculated gear ratio (input speed / output speed) does not match the commanded gear within tolerance. This can be caused by clutch slippage, low fluid, or speed sensor issues.

It is often a precursor to more serious internal damage.
safetyImpact: Slipping can lead to sudden loss of drive.

fixSteps.title: Compare ratios
fixSteps.instruction: Use scanner to log ISS/OSS in each gear.

fixSteps.title: Repair internals
fixSteps.instruction: May require valve body or rebuild.

faq.a: Sometimes — start with fluid and a scan.

title: Gear 1 Incorrect Ratio
fullDescription:
P0731 indicates the transmission is slipping in 1st gear or the speed sensors are reporting an invalid ratio for 1st. Usually caused by worn 1st gear clutches, a stuck shift solenoid A, or low fluid.

Ignoring the code can lead to internal damage.
safetyImpact: Slipping in 1st can prevent normal launches.

fixSteps.title: Solenoid test
fixSteps.instruction: Command solenoid A on with scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Internal repair
fixSteps.instruction: Valve body or rebuild as needed.

faq.a: No — slipping accelerates damage.

title: Gear 2 Incorrect Ratio
fullDescription:
P0732 sets when the TCM detects 2nd-gear ratio errors. Symptoms include slip on 1-2 upshift or flare during light acceleration. Causes are similar to P0731 but specific to the 2nd-gear clutch and shift solenoid B.

Verify fluid first; many P0732 codes resolve with a fluid service if caught early.
safetyImpact: Slipping may cause loss of acceleration.

fixSteps.title: Fluid check
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm proper level and ATF spec.

faq.a: Yes — early action can avoid a full rebuild.

title: Gear 3 Incorrect Ratio
fullDescription:
P0733 indicates 3rd-gear ratio is incorrect during driving. The TCM compares input/output speeds during commanded 3rd gear and flags a mismatch. Slipping clutches and worn drums are common.

Fluid analysis can reveal clutch material, indicating internal wear.
safetyImpact: Mid-range slipping may surprise the driver.

fixSteps.title: Fluid analysis
fixSteps.instruction: Check for burnt smell or debris.

faq.a: Sometimes — but worn clutches are more common at this stage.

title: Gear 4 Incorrect Ratio
fullDescription:
P0734 sets when the TCM detects 4th-gear slip or invalid ratio. In overdrive (or direct on 4-speed boxes), this often shows as engine flare on highway acceleration.

A stuck TCC or worn 3-4 clutch are common causes.
safetyImpact: Slipping at highway speed can be disconcerting.

fixSteps.title: Service fluid
fixSteps.instruction: Drain, inspect, refill with correct ATF.

faq.a: No — slip is mechanical wear, not friction modifier.

title: Gear 5 Incorrect Ratio
fullDescription:
P0735 sets on 5+ speed transmissions when 5th-gear ratio is invalid. Often appears alongside P0734 on units sharing 4-5 clutches.

Diagnose with ratio data and fluid analysis.
safetyImpact: Highway slipping reduces control.

fixSteps.title: Capture ratios
fixSteps.instruction: Scan tool log of all gears.

faq.a: Yes — typically 5+ speed automatics.

title: Reverse Incorrect Ratio
shortDescription: Reverse-gear ratio is out of spec.
fullDescription:
P0736 sets when the transmission appears to slip in reverse or the ratio doesn't match the commanded reverse gear. Symptoms include delayed engagement, no-reverse, or harsh slam into R.

Commonly the result of worn reverse clutch or low fluid in front-wheel-drive automatics.
safetyImpact: No reverse can leave the vehicle stranded.

fixSteps.title: Pressure test
fixSteps.instruction: Hook up gauge to reverse clutch port.

faq.a: Sometimes if low — but worn clutch usually needs rebuild.

title: TCM Engine Speed Output Circuit
shortDescription: TCM cannot drive engine-speed output to PCM.
fullDescription:
P0737 indicates the TCM-to-PCM engine speed signal output is malfunctioning. On some platforms the TCM mirrors engine RPM to the PCM as a sanity check.

The fault is usually a wiring open/short or an internal driver in the TCM.
safetyImpact: Possible degraded shift quality.

fixSteps.title: Replace TCM
fixSteps.instruction: If output driver failed, replace and program.

faq.a: No — usually a wiring or TCM hardware failure.

title: TCM Engine Speed Output Circuit Low
shortDescription: TCM engine speed output reads low/grounded.
fullDescription:
P0738 indicates the TCM's engine speed output signal is stuck low. PCM cannot validate engine RPM via the TCM signal.

A short to ground in the output wire or an internal TCM fault is most likely.
safetyImpact: Shift quality may degrade.

causes.cause: Short to ground in output wire

faq.a: Generally yes — but get it diagnosed soon.

title: Torque Converter Clutch Stuck Off
shortDescription: TCC fails to apply when commanded.
fullDescription:
P0741 sets when the TCM commands torque converter clutch lockup but does not see the expected reduction in slip across the converter. The clutch is mechanically stuck off or the lockup circuit is faulty.

Likely causes include a stuck TCC solenoid, worn converter clutch lining, or valve body wear.
safetyImpact: Reduced fuel economy and possible overheating on highway.

faq.a: Yes for short trips, but expect lower MPG and higher transmission temps.

title: Torque Converter Clutch Stuck On
fullDescription:
P0742 indicates the TCM cannot release the torque converter clutch when commanded. The vehicle stalls coming to a stop because the engine is locked to the transmission output.

A stuck TCC solenoid valve, sticking valve body bore, or contaminated fluid are typical causes.
safetyImpact: Engine stalls at stops — hazardous in traffic.

fixSteps.title: Fluid service
fixSteps.instruction: Drain, inspect, refill with correct ATF.

faq.a: TCC stuck on means engine cannot decouple from drivetrain at stop.

title: Shift Solenoid A Malfunction
fullDescription:
P0750 sets when the TCM detects an electrical fault on shift solenoid A — open, short, or out-of-range resistance. Solenoid A typically controls the 1-2 or 2-3 shift.

Fix usually requires dropping the pan and replacing the solenoid pack.
safetyImpact: Harsh or missed shifts.

faq.a: Usually no — solenoid replacement only.

title: Shift Solenoid B Malfunction
fullDescription:
P0755 indicates an electrical fault on shift solenoid B. Symptoms typically include missed 2-3 or 3-4 shifts depending on platform.

Replace the solenoid and verify wiring integrity.
safetyImpact: Missed shifts may surprise driver.

faq.a: Different solenoid — same diagnostic approach.

title: Shift Solenoid C Malfunction
fullDescription: P0760 sets when solenoid C — generally controlling the 3-4 or 4-5 shift — has an electrical fault. Diagnose and replace as with other shift solenoids.
safetyImpact: Missed shifts at highway speed.

faq.a: Yes — solenoids wear with mileage.

title: Shift Solenoid D Malfunction
fullDescription: P0765 indicates an electrical fault on shift solenoid D. Common on 5+ speed automatics. Replace and verify wiring.
safetyImpact: Missed top-gear shifts and reduced fuel economy.

faq.a: P0770 is solenoid E.

title: Shift Solenoid E Malfunction
fullDescription: P0770 sets on transmissions equipped with a fifth shift solenoid (E). Behaviour and diagnosis mirror other solenoid faults.
safetyImpact: Possible missed shifts.

faq.a: Yes — typically.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Malfunction
fullDescription:
P0775 indicates the secondary pressure control solenoid (B) has an electrical malfunction. PCS B regulates line/clutch pressure on certain shifts.

Failure causes harsh or soft shifts depending on direction of fault.
safetyImpact: Harsh shifts may startle the driver.

faq.a: PCS modulates pressure; shift solenoid switches flow path.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Performance/Stuck Off
fullDescription:
P0776 sets when PCS B is electrically OK but mechanically stuck in the off position, leading to incorrect line pressure.

Valve body cleaning or replacement is often required.
safetyImpact: Slipping and harsh shifts.

faq.a: Sometimes — but mechanical sticking usually needs disassembly.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Stuck On
fullDescription:
P0777 sets when PCS B is mechanically stuck on, producing higher than commanded pressure. Harsh shifts and elevated line pressure result.

Valve body service is the typical fix.
safetyImpact: Harsh, jerky shifts.

faq.a: Short trips OK; harsh shifts can damage mounts.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Electrical
fullDescription:
P0778 indicates an electrical fault — open, short, or out-of-range resistance — on the pressure control solenoid B circuit.

Diagnose with a multimeter and FSM spec.
safetyImpact: Harsh shifts and slipping.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Swap PCS B with pan drop.

faq.a: Often — check before replacing solenoid.

title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit
fullDescription:
P0791 sets when the TCM cannot read the intermediate shaft speed sensor signal. The ISS is critical for ratio calculations.

Usually a sensor failure or harness issue.
safetyImpact: Erratic shifting.

faq.a: Possible — inspect when sensor is out.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Circuit Low
fullDescription:
P0798 indicates the third pressure control solenoid C circuit reads low — likely an open, short to ground, or solenoid failure.

Typical fix is solenoid replacement after wiring inspection.
safetyImpact: Harsh shifts.

faq.a: P0797 is performance/stuck off; P0798 is circuit low.
